biography.plain_text: Peter Fortune is an American financial economist and Tufts University professor emeritus. His scholarship spans municipal debt, equity-market behaviour and derivatives, informed by sustained work with the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston. With his wife, Joan, he later funded a permanent academic chair supporting economics teaching and research at Tufts.

long_biography.plain_text:
Fortune joined Tufts in 1977 and went on to chair its economics department. His work connected public-finance theory with practical questions about tax-exempt bonds, market efficiency and derivative securities. Relationships with economists at the Boston Fed also helped him bring monetary policy and corporate-finance perspectives into the university's curriculum.

Fortune retired from Tufts in 1995 and became a senior consultant to the central bank, a role he held for more than a decade. His later support for an endowed economics chair created a continuing institutional contribution. The chair's inaugural holder was Marcelo Bianconi, a longtime Tufts professor and economics-department chair.
